beats.1: A transaction is a sequence of database operations forming one logical unit of work. Bank transfer is the classic example: debit A and credit B must behave together.
beats.2: Active → Partially committed → Committed. Failure path: Failed → Aborted → restart/terminate.
beats.3: Atomicity = all-or-nothing. Consistency = integrity rules remain valid. Isolation = concurrent transactions behave under the chosen isolation guarantee. Durability = committed effects survive later failure subject to the DBMS guarantee.
beats.4: BEGIN/START TRANSACTION groups statements. COMMIT makes them durable. ROLLBACK undoes uncommitted work. SAVEPOINT creates an intermediate rollback point.
beats.5: Read Uncommitted may permit dirty reads. Read Committed prevents ordinary dirty reads. Repeatable Read gives stronger repeated-read guarantees; phantom behavior varies by DBMS. Serializable is the strongest standard level and aims for serial-equivalent behavior.
beats.6: Definition → bank transfer → four properties with one line + example each → SQL transaction support → isolation levels → conclude with reliability and correctness.
